To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a fast scanning, open-path, TDLAS hyrometer using retro- reflective foils for 2-D concentration field measurements.
the presented TDLAS spectrometers are able to measure the absolute 2-D concentration field of H2O with high precision and accuracy in a spatial area of 80 × 80 cm2 with 2.5 measurements per second.
we developed a fast, robust and easy to use instrument for tomographic 2D-concentration field measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a fast and robust TDLAS hydrometer for tomographic recon- structions of 2-D water vapour concentration profiles.
the development of new methods and instruments for the measurement of greenhouse gas emission in the field, especially for CO2 and CH4.
the development of a fast, robust and low-cost instrument to measure 2-D water vapour concentration fields in environmental research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented instrument is a robust, fast and accurate instrument for 2-D water concentration field measurements in environmental science.
the presented instrument is a good candidate for tomographic reconstrutions of 2-D H2O fields.
the instrument is suitable for tomographic 2D water vapor concentration field mapping with high temporal resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presented instrument is a robust, fast, and low cost instrument that can be used for fast 2-D water concentration field measurements in environmental sciences and can serve as a good basis to be further developed for other applications.
we have successfully developed a robust and easy-to-use TDLAS instrument for 2-D tomographic measurements of water vapor in the field.
the instrument can be considered as robust, easy to set up and a promising instrument to measure 2-D-concentrations of water vapor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of polygon-mirrors with retro-reflective foil is an excellent way to realize fast, open-path TDI-LAS systems with low cost.
the presented instrument can be used as a tomographic scanner in the laboratory as well as in the field.
the use of polygon mirrors and retro-reflective foil can provide a cost-efficient and robust alternative to the use of moving mirrors in TDLAS instruments.
